Maria (CS): Quick sync - Nimbus dedicated bring-up tomorrow 09:00 PT. I want a short checklist here: final quota numbers, autoscale policy, load test plan, and customer enablement steps. Kai, can you confirm the peak concurrency expectation?
AJ (Platform): We have draft quotas: reserved 240 concurrent sessions, burst pool to 400 for 10m. Will that cover the marketing burst?
Kai (Customer): yes, marketing push expects short spikes up to ~380 concurrent users for ~5-8 minutes at launch. Steady-state expected ~160.
Liam (SRE): Ok, plan to pre-warm KV cache and run a ramp for 30m then 2h steady at 80% of reserved. Autoscale policy: scale-up at 70% sustained for 2m, scale-down after 10m at <50%. Thoughts?
Nina (ML Eng): That autoscale window seems conservative but good for quality stability. Also suggest a fallback model variant (smaller quantized) configured for fallback at 95% queue depth.
Maria (CS): Good call on fallback. AJ, can you confirm fallback model is registered and compatible with API routing?
AJ (Platform): Fallback model is rdx-bert-4q (compatible). Routing rule will be: prefer rdx-main, if latency > 800ms or queue depth > 90% then route to rdx-bert-4q. I’ll push canary policy to infra.
Maria (CS): Load script — Liam, can you paste the k6 snippet we'll use?
Liam (SRE): Sure, here's the minimal ramp script we'll run from staging agents:
```
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';
export let options = { stages: [ { duration: '10m', target: 50 }, { duration: '20m', target: 240 }, { duration: '2h', target: 240 }, { duration: '10m', target: 0 } ], thresholds: { 'http_req_duration': ['p(95)<1000'] } };
export default function() { http.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate', JSON.stringify({prompt:'hello'}), { headers: { 'Content-Type':'application/json', 'Authorization':'Bearer $TOKEN' } }); sleep(0.2); }
```
Maria (CS): Perfect. We'll run one full warmup tonight (non-prod) and the production warmup tomorrow 08:00 PT.
deploy-bot: warmup-run-staging-1 finished: status=SUCCESS peak_qps=372 avg_p95=820ms errors=0
Nina (ML Eng): Results look good. p95 under 1s and peak qps close to expected burst. Did we see any KV cache misses?
Liam (SRE): Cache hit rate 94% after 20m; initial misses during ramp as expected. No OOM events. CPU on GPUs hit ~85% at peak for two nodes.
AJ (Platform): One action - tweak autoscale cooldown: scale-down window to 7m to avoid slow shrink during prolonged steady. Thoughts?
Maria (CS): Ok accept tweak. Also need customer enablement checklist: 1) API keys & roles verified, 2) dashboard access for Kai, 3) runbook with rollback steps, 4) post-launch monitoring window 48h. Kai, can your team confirm dashboard access?
Kai (Customer): Confirmed, dashboard access granted to my ops@nimbus team. We'll have an on-call for the 48h window.
Maria (CS): Great. Final action list: AJ -> push routing + cooldown change (ETA: tonight 22:00 PT), Liam -> run prod warmup at 08:00 PT and monitor cache + GPU metrics (ETA: tomorrow 08:00-10:30), Nina -> validate fallback model regression test (ETA: tonight), Maria -> send operations playbook and customer runbook (ETA: 18:00 PT).
AJ (Platform): Will do. I’ll post the canary config here when pushed.
Liam (SRE): I’ll also attach the load CSVs to the incident ticket after run.
Maria (CS): Thanks everyone. If anything changes ping this thread. :rocket:
Kai (Customer): Thanks team, excited to go live.
deploy-bot: scheduled-job prod-warmup queued for 2024-11-05T15:00:00Z
